To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we report the first examples of the hexa-coordinated meso-aryl Sn(IV) dipyrin complexes.

we synthesized and characterized first examples of SnCl2 complexes of meso-substituted aryl dipyrrins, which are stable in solution, have interesting electrochemical properties, and can be used as precursors for the synthesis of Sn(IV)-based dyes.
the first examples of meso-aryldipyrrin complexes of tin(IV) are synthesized and characterized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of meso-aryldipyrrins, their Sn(IV) and Pd(II) complexes and their application in the synthesis of porphyrins and other macrocycles.
the synthesis of meso-substituted dipyrrins, their metal complexes and their application as catalysts in the oxidation of alcohols.
the synthesis and characterization of meso-aryldipyrrin complexes of Sn(IV).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have successfully synthesized the first examples of meso-aryldipyrrin Sn(IV) complex and have characterized them in detail.
the Sn(IV)-dipyrrin complexes are stable in the solid state and in solution and are promising candidates for further investigation as catalysts in organic synthesis.
Sn(IV) meso-aryl complexes of dipyrrins can be easily prepared and isolated in pure form by treating meso-substituted dipyrrin with SnCl2·H2O in the presence of pyridine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Sn(IV)-meso-aryl dypyrrins are the first examples of such complexes, and they are the first examples to have been isolated and fully characterized.
the Sn(IV)-dipyrrin complex has been successfully prepared and the first example of such a complex is reported.
we were able to synthesize the first examples of meso-aryldipyrrin complexes of Sn(IV), and the complex is hexacoordinated with overall appearance of the butterfly like structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Sn(IV) ions can be used to form stable and well-defined complexes with meso-aryl substituted dipyrrins.
Sn(IV) ions are able to coordinate to dipyrrins in a manner analogous to the more commonly studied Zn(II) complexes.
the Sn(IV)-dipyrrin bond is very strong and the dipyrrin is not released in aqueous media.
